source.cleaned_file: goldbound/004 - We Got An Ultra Rare Drop In Elwynn... Is It Enough To Escape？ - Goldbound Episode 4.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Check the link down below for your summer reads. And let's get back to the grind. I decided to kick off the week by testing something classic. The Fargo Deep Mine. Now, this is a quest zone and nothing special at first glance. I was just going to scout for some linen cloth, cobalt mining mallets, and maybe something sneaky worth farming. But only a few minutes into the preliminary tests, something dropped. Might be the lowest drop rate I've ever knowingly received. Now, don't get me wrong. I wish I could say it was a random world drop epic, a T-Boo's blazing long sword, or anything that would command some insane gold. But in Goldbound, where every item has to come from our own hands with no trades, no boosts, quality of life items can be just as valuable in a different way. And while we were scouting through the mine, we looted the Journeyman's backpack, a 14 slot bag. I was doing preliminary research and wasn't recording when it dropped, but the loot appraiser was on and it's in the bag and we got it from the cobalt miners. Now, it's safe to say that in retail wow, a 14 slot bag doesn't exactly turn heads, but here for Goldilocked in the zones we're locked to right now. And compared to our great picking six slot sack and those massive eight slot collector bags, this thing is huge. And if you've ever played classic WoW, you know looting a bag in a starting zone is a rush. And this is basically a runcloth bag drop in Elwin.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/004 - We Got An Ultra Rare Drop In Elwynn... Is It Enough To Escape？ - Goldbound Episode 4.en-orig.txt
source.quote: So according to Wowhead, the journeyman's backpack is a relatively rare drop from dungeon bosses and elite mobs. But the drop we got was from a cobalt miner. And get this, across all of the logged cobalt minor kills on Wowhead, there have only been two recorded drops out of 305,000 kills. That's a 0.000065% drop rate. Actually insane. More room for copper ore, more room for peace bloom, and more room for profit. With some extra bag space and a pipe dream of rare loot tables, I figured it was time to test out one of Elwin's most classic and deadly mobs, the Murloc. Now, there are three main spawn zones for these guys. You'll find them around the islands in Crystal Lake, east of Stone Karen Lake, and down south near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. You'll find a mix of regular murlocs, murloc foragers, murloc lurkers, and if you're lucky, a murloc tide runner or two. Their loot tables across all these variants are mostly the same with a few different percentage points here and there. So really, any of the three farm spots will work. And better yet, these mobs do actually hypers spawn in all of the locations. That means with just a bit of movement, you never run out of anything to kill. Sounds perfect, right? Well, except it isn't. After just about 3 to 5 minutes of farming in a single location, I noticed something odd. You see, linen cloth stopped dropping. It's a pretty high drop rate, and I was partially just farming these murlocs to get some more cloth to make some more shirts. We also stopped getting grays and greens. All we were getting from the drops was silence, a few murloc fins, and clamshells. Now, it turns out this isn't just bad RNG.

source.quote: It's actually a known issue in the current patch of retail. A bug that apparently nukes loot tables in open world farms after only a few minutes of mob grinding. Kazaki wrote about this on the forums. And from our own testing, yeah, it doesn't look like it's fixed yet. This is a pretty big issue for openw world crafting reagent farms. So, to try to counter it, I started rotating between all three spawn locations, hoping that changing the region would reset the drop rate. It kind of helped for a few kills, but not really. So, I called it after 30 minutes. And here was the hall. 120 barnacled clams, 205 murloc fins, only 35 linen cloth, a handful of copper ore and malchite, and eight gray and white items. Most of which will just be vendor trash, but a few will go into the transmog bank for reposting later because they have a decent sell rate and average list price.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/004 - We Got An Ultra Rare Drop In Elwynn... Is It Enough To Escape？ - Goldbound Episode 4.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Now, the fun part, the clams. When opened, these guys have about a 5% drop rate for pearls. Nothing groundbreaking, and while they only go for 10 gold each, it's not bad to stockpile them on Goldilock in case we need them for a future crafting recipe. All in all, turns out not to be a very lucrative method. Decent for cooking reagents, some white gear, and a little sprinkle of crafting mats, but nothing to write home about. The fins and clam meat will probably sell for about 30 gold total, but honestly, I might just bank them for some cooking XP down the road. In short, murloc farming is not the wave. At least not until Blizzard fixes the loot bug. We gave it a fair chance. But for now, we're going to go ahead and move on. So, I decided to give blacksmithing a go. Up until now, we haven't really touched it.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/004 - We Got An Ultra Rare Drop In Elwynn... Is It Enough To Escape？ - Goldbound Episode 4.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Mostly because copper ore, copper bars, and copper bolts have been some of our best sellers. Why mess with what's working, right? But with the grind in full swing and the auction shelf starting to feel a little repetitive, I figured it was time to expand. Get a few new pieces in the rotation and maybe turn some of that excess copper into something people might actually wear. So, first things first, the materials. I went out and gathered all that we'd need for the beginning of blacksmithing crafts. Obviously, the main ingredient is going to be copper ore smelted into bars. Some of the swords and two-handers actually eat up over 10 bars each, which starts to add up pretty fast when you're batch crafting like this. I also noticed that we needed light leather for a few recipes, presumably for the handles. I mean, the game doesn't really explain it, but that's what it says, so that's what we got to get. And by popular demand from episode 3, yep, we're going back to the boar farm. At least this time, we're here with a purpose and not just grinding for its own sake. We're farming leather that might actually turn a profit. So, after a few hours of farming, skinning, and smelting, we had everything we needed. Enough copper, enough leather. So, let's get to crafting. And as we're crafting away, it feels like a good moment to talk about professions and how they're going to work in the series. Right now, in Elwin, things are pretty simple. We're working with level one materials, early recipes, and low skill caps. That means it's easy to bounce between gathering and production professions without much friction or time sync. Take this blacksmithing run. We cap out at 75 skill in just a few minutes of crafting.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/004 - We Got An Ultra Rare Drop In Elwynn... Is It Enough To Escape？ - Goldbound Episode 4.en-orig.txt
source.quote: A couple stacks of ore, some light leather, a vendor hammer, and that's it. We're done. But looking ahead, I can already see the problem brewing. Eventually, we're going to hit recipes in later zones that require 250 or even 300 blacksmithing. And that's where things will get tricky. Training that high with limited zone access is going to be a serious investment in both materials and time. One solution, of course, would be to open up a gold bound war band, spin up some alts with specialized crafting rules, and honestly, it would probably be pretty fun. We could build a whole little economy that way, but that's not what this challenge is about. From day one, this has been Goldilocks journey. One character, one zone at a time. No shortcuts and no sidekicks. So, going forward, we'll probably have to treat production professions more like seasonal grinds. focus on them in bulk when we've got the materials, the access, and the levels, and then stockpile what we make and sell it off slowly over time. I'm sure that we'll throw more than a few spanners in the works, and we're probably going to hit some walls and some crafting dead ends, but hey, that's gold bound. Okay, so the current blacksmithing in the end, we pretty much just crafted two or three of everything that we had access to. Kept it pretty simple. The weapons though, they seem to really stand out. Solid item values, decent sell rates, and even though they're low level, I wouldn't be surprised if a few of them actually got picked up by leveling alts. Is it likely? Probably not, but possible.

source.quote: Either way, we ended up with a good handful of extra items and a ton of item value from just this little blacksmithing shuffle. Now, this won't be something we do every single day. Most of the green weapons already require a decently high blacksmith something level, but we'll keep an eye on what sells. And if something actually moves quickly, we'll restock it when it makes sense. For now, it's just another inventory on the auction house to sit and wait for a couple buyers. Anyways, if you've watched episode 1, it's time to revisit some classic farms with some marginal improvements. Now, the first farm I want to circle back to is the frayed knot. And yeah, with the spike in supply from the series, the prices have dropped. But interestingly, the seller rate is way up. It's no longer acting like a high-priced slow mover. Instead, it's trading more like a mid-priced, moderately fast mover. According to TSM, regionwide sales are clocking in at over 200 per day. Even at just 200 gold, that's still 40,000 gold in daily volume in the region. Now, I do have a hunch that some of that is people maybe trying to reset the market back up to 500 or a,000 gold, but hey, a free market is a free market. And if we can sell 200, we'll sell 200. So, how do we get them?

source.quote: And again, if you remember from episode 1, this whole gold making method revolves around reselling Donna's cats on the auction house. It's simple and it's charming and only mildly deranged. But there's actually a neat little trick you can do after you've bought the cats in crates. Have a good one. The game treats new and I guess you could call them used cats differently. If you right click the crate to learn the pet and then open your pet journal, you can select the cat and choose to put it back in a cage. And then if you check the bags, the cat is back, but this time it's flagged as a different item. And the auction house and TSM sale data shows a separate listing for the caged version the crate version. And since these cats are basically Goldilock's only companions in Elwin, I figured we should add one to the series. So, meet Goldieat. From now on, whenever we're pickpocking through the woods, we might have little orange tag on. But back to the sales. When we check the auction house, both the caged cat and the crate cat are actually listed separately and with different prices. And the weird part, the caged cats, aka the used cats, often sell for more. Now, this is probably because not everyone knows the difference, but this trick lets us list both versions, doubling our market presence and doubling our chances to sell. Not bad for a couple silver and a trip to our good friend Donas. Now, it wouldn't be a goldbound episode without a bit of dual gathering, but since we've already minaxed the routes last episode, we're not here to test the gold per hour. This run is more about capitalizing on the clean gathers and soaking in the ambiance. And honestly, it's the perfect time for a little fireside chat. Let's talk about the series and more importantly what comes next. As you know, we are somewhat on the cusp of unlocking our next zone. And by the end of this episode, we'll know if we made it or if there's still a little bit left in that threshold. But either way, it's time to think ahead.

source.quote: Still, I'm keeping my eye on those drop rates because something isn't adding up. But with all this extra space, let's craft up something we might be able to sell for a little more profit. And by the way, all this gathering, it wasn't just for B-roll. This time around, we actually focused a bit more on herbs than usual. Now, back in episode 3, we ran a full dual gathering test. And honestly, we determined that herbs weren't even worth picking up. And the culprit was alabaster pigments. I'd gone through every recipe I could learn from the trade skill trainers in Elwin, and nearly all of them just turned those pigments into Moonglow ink and those into squirrels that sold for nothing. And while Moonglow Ink can sometimes trade for double the price of alabaster, the market's a little unstable. So, I wrote it off. But this past weekend, while I was cutting weight for a powerlifting meet, just passing the time in Owen, I started theory crafting, looking for new, overlooked, and novel ways to turn a profit. And I think we found one. And there's a reason I left this farm for the latter half of the video. I wanted to make sure only the dedicated goldbound viewers made it this far, because this might be one of those little tricks that only works for a few days before the market catches on. So, here's what I found. Low-level inscription in Elwin doesn't just offer recipes from trainers. It actually has a discovery system built in.
